Compound 2 also exhibits a 3D framework. Moreover, the two compounds both exhibit strong solid-state fluorescence emissions at room temperature. Furthermore, the 1, 4-NDC ligand is a good antenna ligand for Eu(III), when introduced the Eu(III) ions into 1 to get hybrid framework 1', the hybrid material 1' shows strong red luminescence and the temperature-dependent luminescent properties studies indicate that 1' is a potential luminescent thermometer in the range from 270 to 400 K.

Article Title: A luminescent barium-based metal-organic framework: Synthesis, structure and efficient detection of 4-nitrobenzoic acid
Author Keywords: Barium(II) complex; Carboxylate substituted anthracene; Metal-organic frameworks; Nitroaromatics detection
Keywords Plus: NITROAROMATIC COMPOUNDS; COORDINATION POLYMERS; PHOTOLUMINESCENCE; MUTAGENICITY; BA
Abstract: The assembly of a carboxylate substituted anthracene derivative with barium(II) salt yielded a 3D luminescent metal-organic framework [Ba-2(adda)(2)(H(2)adda)(H2O)(2)](n) 1 (H(2)adda = (2E,2'E)-3,3'-(anthracene-9,10-diyl) diacrylic acid), which was structurally characterized by elemental analysis, powdered and single-crystal X-ray diffraction. Compound 1 exhibits a turn on luminescence response toward 4-nitrobenzoic acid (4-NBA) different from most nitroaromatic compounds displaying a turn-off luminescence stimulus. Increasing luminescence intensities with addition of 4-NBA in 1 dispersed in DMF are attributed to the dissociation of H(2)adda, evidenced by H-1 NMR. Compound 1 is effective as a potential 4-NBA detector by establishing the relationship between the luminescence intensity of 1 and the molar concentration of 4-NBA.

Article Title: A 3,6-connected 3-D arsenotungstate framework based on unique sandwich-type metal-organic dimer chain
Author Keywords: Hydrothermal synthesis; Keggin arsenotungstate; Photocatalytic properties; Electrocatalytic behavior
Keywords Plus: KEGGIN; POLYOXOMETALATE; CLUSTERS; HYBRIDS
Abstract: A 3-D inorganic-organic network based on kiggen-type arsenotungstat, [Ag(4,4'-bpy)](2)[{Ag(4,4'-bpy)}2((AsW11WO40)-W-VI-O-V)]center dot 3H(2)O(1) (4,4'-bpy = 4,4'-bipyridine), has been synthesized by hydrothermal means. X-ray single crystal analysis shows that compound 1 contains two crystallography independent silver ions, which adopt different coordination modes connecting bpy ligand alternately to form two kinds of metal-organic chains {Agbpy}(n). Two parallel {Ag(1)bpy}(n) chains are linked together via {ASW(12)O(40)} linkers to result in a unique sandwich-type dimer chain along a axis. Each Keggin cluster on sandwich chain bonds with six cognate clusters on six adjacent sandwich chains via surrounding six Ag, forming a 2-D layer along c axis. The 2D layer and 1D sandwich chains are intersected to yield a 3D network with 1-D channel. The {Ag(2)bpy}(n) chains and lattice water reside in the channel and further stabilize the 3-D framework via H-bonding and pi-pi accumulation. From topological perspective, compound 1 can be viewed as a 3, 6-connected network with {4(3)}(2){4(6).6(6).8(3)} topology. Compound 1 shows merit electrocatalytic activity for reduction of H2O2 and efficient catalytic degradation ability for three typical dyes under UV radiation.

Article Title: A series of lanthanide coordination polymers based on flexible bis-(imidazole-4,5-dicarboxylate) ligand: Syntheses, structures and fluorescent properties
Author Keywords: Lanthanide; Crystal structure; Topology; Irnidazole-4,5-dicarbcocylic acid; Luminescence
Keywords Plus: METAL-ORGANIC FRAMEWORKS; LUMINESCENCE; EMISSION; PHOTOLUMINESCENCE; COMPLEXES; TB(III); EU(III); FE3+
Abstract: A series of lanthanide coordination polymers, namely {[Ln(HL)(H2O)(2)].H2O}n (Ln = Ce(1), Pr(2), Nd(3), Eu(4) and Tb(5); H4L = 1,1'-(propane-1,3-diyl)bis(1H-imidazole-4,5-dicarboxylic acid)) have been synthesized under hydrothermal conditions and characterized by infrared spectroscopy, element analysis, single-crystal X-ray diffraction, powder X-ray diffraction and thermogravimetric analyses. These isostructural complexes exhibit 3D framework with a sra topology built by HL3- anions mu(4)-bridging metal ions through two IDC groups it different coordination modes. The luminescent property of complexes containing Eu(III) and Tb(III) have also been investigated in detail.

Article Title: Auxiliary ligand-assisted structural variation of two Co(II) metal-organic frameworks: Syntheses, crystal structure and magnetic properties
Author Keywords: Co(II)-MOFs; Crystal structure; Polycarboxylate; Pyridine-based linear ligand; Magnetic property
Keywords Plus: COORDINATION POLYMERS; ARCHITECTURES; NETWORKS; CO
Abstract: Two Co(II)-containing complexes, (Co-6(SO4)(2)(BTEC)(OH)(4)center dot 3H(2)O], (1) and [Co-2(BTEC)(4-bpdb)(H2O)(2)center dot 4H(2)O](r) (2) (H4BTEC = 1,2,4,5-benzenetetracarboxylic acid; 4-bpdb = 1,4-bis(4-pyridyI)-2,3-diaza-1,3-butadiene) have been successfully synthesized. Single crystal X-ray diffraction analysis reveals that complex 1 exhibits a 3D intricate framework, whereas 2 features a pillared-layer with (4,5)-connected net topology. Magnetic studies demonstrate that antiferromagnet and weak ferromagnetism behaviour are observed in 1 and 2, respectively.

Article Title: A unique (4,4,5)-connected 3D zinc (II) metal-organic framework for highly efficient photodegradation of Rhodamine B under UV light
Author Keywords: Crystal structure; Hydrothermal synthesis; Metal-organic framework; Photocatalytic degradation; Semi-rigid bis(benzimidazole); Zinc (II)
Keywords Plus: COORDINATION POLYMERS; 5-NITRO-1,2,3-BENZENETRICARBOXYLIC ACID; SONOCHEMICAL SYNTHESIS; STRUCTURAL DIVERSITY; LUMINESCENCE; CONSTRUCTION; NICKEL(II); COBALT(II); TOPOLOGIES; COMPLEXES
Abstract: A new zinc (II) metal-organic framework, [Zn-3(L)(2)(nbta)(2)](n) (1) (L = 1,4-bis(benzimidazol-1-yl)-2-butene, H(3)nbta = 5-nitro-1,2,3-benzenetricarboxylic acid) was hydrothermally synthesized and structural characterized. 1 possesses a unique 3D (4,4,5)-connected network with a Schlafla symbol of {4(2).6(3).8}(2){4(4).6(2)}{4(7).6(3)}(2). Furthermore, the photocatalytic property of 1 for degradation of the Rhodamine B (RhB) was examined under UV irradiation.

Article Title: A novel photosensitizing decatungstate-based MOF: Synthesis and photocatalytic oxidation of cyclohexane with molecular oxygen
Author Keywords: Polyoxometalate; Decatungstate; Metal-organic framework; Photocatalysis; Cyclohexane
Keywords Plus: METAL-ORGANIC FRAMEWORK; SILICA; ALKYLATION; CATALYSTS
Abstract: The reaction of [(n-C4H9)(4)N](4)[W10O32], 3-amino-4,4'-bipyridine (NPY) and Cu(ClO4)(2)center dot 6H(2)O by a diffusion method led to a novel 3D decatungstate-based MOF {[Cu(NPY)(2)(DMF)](2)(W10O32)}center dot DMF center dot 3CH(3)CN (referred to as DT-NPY) with 1D hydrophilic/hydrophobic channels, which was structurally characterized by elemental analyses, IR spectrum, UV-Vis spectrum, powder X-ray diffraction (XRD) and single-crystal X-ray diffraction. DT-NPY exhibits remarkable photocatalytic activities for the oxidation of cyclohexane to cyclohexanone and cyclohexanol by molecular oxygen under mild conditions. The high catalytic efficiency, high stability and good recyclability of the photocatalyst DT-NPY demonstrates the superiority of the decatungstate imbedded MOF over homogeneous systems and other heterogenization methods.

Article Title: A multifunctional anionic 3D Cd(II)-MOF derived from 2D layers catenation: Organic dyes adsorption, cycloaddition of CO2 with epoxides and luminescence
Author Keywords: Metal-organic frameworks; Dye adsorption; Catalysis; Luminescence
Keywords Plus: FACILE SYNTHESIS; SELECTIVE CO2; METAL; FRAMEWORK; SEPARATION; REMOVAL; DESIGN; CARBON; SITES
Abstract: An anionic Cd(II)-based metal-organic framework, {[Cd(L)(bpb)(0.5)(H2O)]center dot H2O center dot[(CH3)(2)NH2](+)}(n) (HL-7, HL is the initial of the author Hui-Ling Liu; H3L = 2',6'-dimethyl-[1,1'-biphenyl]-3,4',5-tricarboxylic acid and bpb = 1,4-bis(pyrid-4-yl)benzene), has been hydrothermally synthesized and structurally characterized. Interestingly, HL-7 reveals a three dimensional (3D) frameworks which are constructed from catenation of 2D layers. Further studies prove that as an anionic framework, HL-7 could be a good candidate as adsorption materials for cationic organic dyes, such as methylene blue (MB+) and rhodamine B (RhB+). Moreover, catalytic properties for the cycloaddition of CO2 with epoxides and luminescent property of HL-7 are also investigated at normal temperature and pressure.

Article Title: Anion-directed structures and luminescences of two Cu(I) coordination polymers based on bipyrazole
Author Keywords: Luminescence; Copper(I) coordination polymers; Topology; Penetration structure; Anion-directed
Keywords Plus: METAL-ORGANIC FRAMEWORKS; IONS
Abstract: Two anion-directed Cu(I) coordination polymers (CPs), namely, [Cu-2(TMBP)(2)(mu-CN)(I)center dot(3.5H(2)O)(n) (1, TMBP = 3,3',5,5'-tetramethyl-4,4'-bipyrazole) and [Cu-2(TMBP)(2)(mu-SCN)(mu-CN)](n) (2), were synthesized through solvothermal method and characterized by single crystal and powder X-ray diffraction, elemental analysis. 1 is a 3-dimension framework with nanocavity and (4(2).6(3).8) topology while 2 is a 2-dimension network with 3-fold penetration and (6(2).10)(6.6) topology, the difference in structure being related to the anions (I- or SCN-) included in precursor solution. Furthermore, 1 exhibits strong blue emission when excited at 315 nm, which should be resulted from 1 to Cu(I) charge transfer; however, no obvious luminescence was observed in case of 2. This work emphasizes a strategy of anion-directed synthesis of CPs for tuning photoluminescent property.

Article Title: Synthesis of magnesium based metal organic framework by microwave hydrothermal process
Author Keywords: Metal organic framework; Magnesium; X-ray diffraction; SEM; DSC
Keywords Plus: EFFICIENT; REMOVAL; WATER; MOFS
Abstract: A new complex of magnesium and benzene tricarboxylic acid was synthesized via microwave hydrothermal synthesis method. The compounds were characterized with the MD (X-ray diffraction), SEM (scanning electron microscope), FT-IR (Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy) and DSC/TGA (differential scanning calorimetry/thermogravimetric analysis). Highest yield of the compound was obtained at 200 degrees C. The compound synthesized at 220 degrees C was slightly brown in color. The material synthesized at 170 and 200 degrees C were completely soluble in water as compared to the compound synthesized at 220 degrees C which was partially soluble in water.

Article Title: Energy-efficient sonochemical approach for the preparation of nanohybrid composites from graphene oxide and metal-organic framework
Author Keywords: Metal-organic framework; Sonochemistry; Ultrasound; Graphene oxide; Nanohybrid composites
Keywords Plus: ADSORPTION; ULTRASOUND; AMMONIA; NANOPARTICLES; CHEMISTRY; MICROWAVE; LIGANDS; GROWTH; ZIF-8; FILMS
Abstract: Two-fold interpenetration zinc-based metal-organic framework/graphene oxide (TMU-16-NH2/GO) nanohybrid materials were synthesized under a green, simple and large-scale sonochemical preparation method at room temperature and atmospheric pressure. The role of concentrations of graphene oxide on size and morphology of nanostructures TMU-16-NH2/GO hybrid have been studied. The materials were characterized by scanning electron microscopy (SEM), powder X-ray diffraction (PXRD), Fourier transform infrared (FTIR) spectroscopy and nitrogen adsorption. Both of the pure MOF and the nanohybrid MOF/GO composites exhibit microporous structure with a small number of mesopores. TMU-16-NH2 shows type IV isotherm with a H4 hysteresis loop, while the isotherm of TMU-16-NH2/GO appears to show normal Type II adsorption with a Type H3 hysteresis loop. The results obtained demonstrate this method to be applicable to the synthesis of other MOFs/GO nano hybrids and may possibly find various forthcoming industrial and technological applications.

Article Title: One-step synthesis of confined ion Agx-Cu-BTC for selective catalytic reduction of NO with CO
Author Keywords: Porous materials; Crystal growth; One-step synthesis; Microstructure; Cu-BTC
Keywords Plus: METAL-ORGANIC FRAMEWORK; ADSORPTION; COMPOSITES; AMMONIA
Abstract: Ag2O dispersed in Bi-metal organic framework Ag-x-Cu-BTC were firstly prepared by preassembled method (PAM). These catalysts have regular octahedral shape with high specific surface area. In addition, mixed-node Ag-x-Cu-BTC show better performance for CO-SCR with the addition of Ag cations that enhance CO-SCR activity under the same condition at a lower temperature (< 240 degrees C). The addition of Ag cations into metallic framework results in promoting the catalysts activity and increasing reaction activated sites, suggesting that metal organic frameworks should be a promising material for SCR of denitrification. It also promotes a new method for acquiring metal oxides/metal organic frameworks.

Article Title: A bifunctional luminescent Zn(II)-organic framework: Ionothermal synthesis, selective Fe(III) detection and cationic dye adsorption
Author Keywords: Metal-organic framework; Fluorescence; Ionothermal synthesis; Fe(III) detection; Dye adsorption
Keywords Plus: METAL-ORGANIC FRAMEWORK; PICRIC ACID; FE3+; SIZE; MOFS
Abstract: A new 3D metal-organic framework (PMI)(2)[Zn-4(mu(4)-O)Br2L2] (1, PMI = 1-propyl-3-methylimidazolium, H3L = biphenyl-3,4',5-tricarboxylic acid) was prepared from tricarboxylic acid H3L and Zn(NO3)(2) under ionothermal conditions. Single crystal X-ray diffraction analysis reveals that the anionic framework possesses a (3,6)-connected topological network and contains rare {Zn-4(mu(4)-O)Br-2} clusters as building units. The compound was further characterized by powder X-ray diffraction (PXRD), Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR) and thermogravimetric analysis (TGA). Interestingly, 1 can serve as a sensitive and recyclable luminescent probe to detect Fe3+ ions. In addition, 1 can effectively and selectively absorb cationic dyes, possibly due to the anionic nature of the framework.

Article Title: Syntheses, structures and photoluminescence of three Zn(II) coordination polymers based on N-containing heterocyclic ligand and varied auxiliary ligands
Author Keywords: Heterocyclic ligands; Auxiliary ligands; Structural controlling; Topology; Luminescent properties
Keywords Plus: METAL-ORGANIC FRAMEWORK; CRYSTAL-STRUCTURES; CONSTRUCTION; COMPLEXES
Abstract: Three coordination polymers, i.e. [Zn(DIPM)(BDC)](n)center dot n(CH3OH) center dot n(H2O) (1), [Zn(DIPM)(BDC-NH2)](n)center dot 2n(H2O) (2) and [Zn(DIPM)(BDC-OH)]. (3) were obtained by hydrothermal reaction based on zinc nitrate and 4,6-di(1H-imidazol-1-yl)-pyrimidine (DIPM) in the presence of varied auxiliary ligands such as 1,4-naphthalenedicarboxylic acid (H2BDC), 2-amino-1,4-naphthalenedicarboxylic acid (H2BDC-NH2) and 2-hydroxyl-1,4-naphthalenedicarboxylic acid (H2BDC-OH). Their structures have been characterized by single-crystal X-ray diffraction, powder X-ray diffraction (PXRD) and thermogravimetric analysis (TGA). Complex 1 shows a two-dimensional (2D) two-fold interpenetrated network with sql topology, while complexes 2 and 3 exhibit 3D diamond frameworks with four-fold and five-fold interpenetration, respectively. The above results show that the auxiliary ligands have significant influence on the ultimate structures. In addition, the solid-state luminescent properties of 1-3 have also been investigated.

Article Title: A dual-responsive luminescent TbIII-organic framework with high water stability for selective sensing of Fe3+ and Cr2O72- in water systems
Author Keywords: Metal-organic framework; Luminescence; Sensor; Cr2O72-; Fe3+
Keywords Plus: WHITE-LIGHT EMISSION; LEWIS BASIC SITES; GAS-ADSORPTION; TUNABLE COLORS; ACID; MOF; CONSTRUCTION; CATALYSIS; CLUSTERS; DESIGN
Abstract: A novel 3D Tb-III-based MOF {[TbL(H2O)]center dot 2H(2)O}(n) (denoted as 1) was successfully prepared by semi-rigid organic linker 4,4,4 ''-s-triazine-1,3,5-triyltri-m-aminobenzoate (H3L) and Tb-III under hydrothermal synthesis. The fresh 1 was investigated and characterized in detail by single crystal X-ray diffraction, powder X-ray diffraction, Fourier-transform infrared spectrum, elemental analysis, luminescent spectrum, and thermogravimetric analysis, respectively. Thanks to high stability and strong green luminescent properties, the as-synthesized 1 can be considered as a dual-responsive luminescent sensor for Fe3+ and Cr2O72- in aqueous solutions. In addition, it can be recycled at least five runs without any change.

Article Title: A tetrazole-containing triphenylamine-based metal-organic framework: Synthesis and photocatalytic oxidative C-C coupling reaction
Author Keywords: Photocatalysis; Coupling reaction; Metal-organic framework; Triphenylamine-based ligand
Keywords Plus: PHOTOREDOX CATALYSIS; HYDROGEN STORAGE; EFFICIENT; LIGAND; COPPER
Abstract: A novel tetrazole-containing triphenylamine-based MOF {TBA[Cu-2(TPA)]}center dot CH3CN (Cu-TPA; TBA = tetrabutylammonium cation) has been solvothermally synthesized by the reaction of CuCl2 center dot 2H(2)O, tris(4-(2H-tetrazol-5-yl)phenyl)amine (H(3)TPA) and (TBA)(4)[W10O32] and structurally characterized by IR spectrum, UV-Vis spectrum, fluorescence analysis, powder X-ray diffraction (PXRD) and single-crystal X-ray diffraction. More interestingly, Cu-TPA exhibits remarkable heterogeneous photocatalytic property and promotes the oxidative C-C coupling reaction under mild conditions. The high catalytic efficiency, high stability and good recyclability of the photocatalyst Cu-TPA demonstrate the superiority of the tetrazole-containing triphenylamine-based MOF over homogeneous systems and other noble-metal-catalyzed methods.

Article Title: A novel 3D Ag-based metal-organic framework: Synthesis, structure and property
Author Keywords: Metal-organic framework; Cation; CO2; Water; Cr2O72-
Keywords Plus: MOF; ADSORPTION; ETHANOL; CO2
Abstract: A novel 3D Ag-I-based cationic metal-organic framework {[AgL2]center dot BF4}(n) (denoted as 1) can be successfully generated by the assemble process of the neutral organic linker (denoted as L) and AgBF4 under the diffusion method. MOF 1 was further explored and investigated in detail. The resultant 1 exhibits selective adsorption of CO2 and water. In addition, it possesses outstanding water stability and equilibrium anion BF4- in its pores, leading to it can be considered as an ion exchange material for Cr2O72- in aqueous solution.

Article Title: Magnetic ZIF-8 as a stable support for biomolecules via adsorption in aqueous buffered solutions at pH=7
Author Keywords: Metal-organic frameworks; ZIF-8 stability; Buffered media; Biomolecule support; Adsorption
Keywords Plus: METAL-ORGANIC FRAMEWORKS; ZEOLITIC IMIDAZOLATE FRAMEWORK-8; FACILE SYNTHESIS; STABILITY; IMMOBILIZATION; FUNCTIONALITY; MORPHOLOGIES; SIZE; MOFS
Abstract: Metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) have been recently proposed as supports for biomolecules immobilization, particularly for enzymes. However, their stability under the high ionic strength aqueous solutions required for practical applications of these biocatalysts have not been evaluated. Here, it is shown that surface modifications and a careful analysis and selection of the buffer components must be accomplished to ensure the resistance of the MOF to hydrolysis, even for the previously assumed robust Zeolitic Imidazole Frameworks (ZIFs). By taking into account these considerations, and introducing polyvinylpyrrolidone (PVP) as a surfactant in the synthetic process, a resistant and stable magnetic MOF (Fe3O4@7IF-8/PVP) was obtained. Further, the loading capacity of the stabilized synthetized structures for the immobilization of a model protein, such as bovine serum albumin (BSA), was analyzed. It was found that physical interaction provides an efficient and suitable method to immobilize this biomolecule without evidence of leaching.

Article Title: A two-fold interpenetrating metal-organic framework based on [Co4O(COO)6] cluster: Synthesis, crystal structure and catalytic properties
Author Keywords: Metal-Organic Framework; Cobalt cluster; Interpenetrating framework; Heterogeneous catalyst
Keywords Plus: COORDINATION POLYMER; CAPTURE; MOF; LIGAND; CO2
Abstract: One new Metal-Organic Frameworks, [Co4O(L)(2)]center dot(DMF)(8)center dot(H2O)(8) (1, H3L = 4-[N,N-bis(4-methylbenzoic acid) amino]benzoic acid), had been successfully constructed under hydrothermal conditions, which firstly presents the [Co4O(COO)(6)] secondary-building unit similar to the typical [Zn4O(COO)(6)] one via single-crystal X-ray diffraction studies. All of the cobalt ions exhibit the four-coordinate environment, and possess more open metal sites. Heterogeneous catalytic experiments on allylic oxidation of cyclohexene indicate that 1 exhibits high catalytic activity by utilizing the tert-butylhydroperoxide (t-BuOOH) as the oxidant. The activation energy for the whole process of oxidation of cylcohexene had been calculated as 40.6 kJ mol(-1), which indicate the important role of the special [Co4O(COO)(6)] cluster in the resulted heterogeneous catalyst.

Article Title: Two novel 3D MOFs based on the biphenyl-2,4,6,3′,5′-pentacarboxylic acid ligand: Synthesis, crystal structure and luminescence properties
Author Keywords: Metal-organic frameworks; Biphenyl-2; 4; 6; 3 '; 5 '-pentacarboxylic acid; Crystal structure; Luminescent properties
Keywords Plus: METAL-ORGANIC FRAMEWORKS; AGGREGATION-INDUCED EMISSION; COORDINATION POLYMERS; PHOTOLUMINESCENT PROPERTIES; DICARBOXYLATE; TOPOLOGY; UNITS
Abstract: Two novel 3D metal-organic frameworks [Cd-3 (bpbc)(mu(3)-OH)(H2O)(3)]center dot H2O (1) and [Zn2Na (bpbc)(DMF)(1.5)(EtOH)(0.5 )(H2O)(5)]center dot 0.5H(2)O (2) have been synthesized by using biphenyl-2, 4, 6, 3', 5'-pentacarboxylic acid (H(5)bpbc) as the ligand under solvothermal/hydrothermal conditions. The complexes were characterized by elemental analysis, single-crystal X-ray diffraction (XRD), powder X-ray diffraction (PXRD), IR spectra and thermogravimetric analysis (TGA). Structural analysis revealed that complex 1 shows a (5, 10)-connected 3D network based on the [Cd-6 (COO)(10)(mu(3)-OH)(2)] SBUs with unusual topology, while complex 2 exhibits a (3, 3, 6)-connected 3D framework. The structural difference between 1 and 2 indicated that the coordination fashion of bpbc(5-) and the kind of metal ions could play critical role in the construction of MOFs. In addition, new fluorescence emissions were observed for 1 and 2, and the solid state luminescent properties were investigated.

Article Title: L-Proline functionalized metal-organic framework PCN-261 as catalyst for aldol reaction
Author Keywords: MOF; L-Proline; Crystal structure; Porous materials; Catalysis
Keywords Plus: ASYMMETRIC ALDOL; MICHAEL ADDITION
Abstract: A homochiral MOF, PCN-261-NHPro, was prepared via solvothermal synthesis of Fe2CoO(CH3COO)(6) with H(3)tcpb-NHPro. The aldol addition was selected as a model reaction for the estimation of the catalytic performance of the PCN-261-NHPro, which showed reversed diastereomeric selectivity in contrast to homogeneous catalysts.

Article Title: Rapid and efficient ultrasonic-assisted removal of lead(II) in water using two copper- and zinc-based metal-organic frameworks
Keywords Plus: CENTRAL COMPOSITE DESIGN; LOADED ACTIVATED CARBON; GRAPHENE OXIDE; HYDROTHERMAL SYNTHESIS; SELECTIVE DETECTION; ADSORPTION; IONS; DYES; EXTRACTION; SAMPLES
Abstract: Today, water pollution through heavy metal ions is a major concern in all human communities. In this study, two metal-organic frameworks (MOFs), which named by Cu-BTC and Zn-BTC, with benzene-1,3,5-tricarboxylic acid linker, were successfully synthesized. Characterization of these two MOFs was performed using various techniques, such as FT-IR, XRD and SEM analysis. These frameworks have special properties like rapid, efficient and selective removal of metal ions from contaminated water. The use of an ultrasonic device plays an important role in shortening the absorption time of lead(II) ions by increasing the absorbent dispersion in the solution. The adsorption capacity was affected by variables such as pH solution, Pb2+ initial concentration, adsorbent dosage and contact time. For Pb(II) metal ions the sorption capacities of 333 mg g(-1) and 312 mg g(-1) were obtained effectively by Cu-BTC and Zn-BTC structures, respectively. The experimental adsorption data for Cu-BTC and Zn-BTC MOFs, are well suited with the pseudo-second-order kinetic model (R-2 = 0.99), and the adsorption isotherms of Pb2+ metal ions are in good agreement with the Langmuir model. This work exhibits two BTC-based MOFs to remove Pb2+ from pollutant water in < 30 min effectively.

Article Title: Synthesis, characterization and fluorescent properties of two porous lead(II) complexes assembled from similar carboxylphenyl terpyridine polydentate ligands
Author Keywords: Lead(II) complex; Crystal structure; Porous coordination polymers; Fluorescence property
Keywords Plus: METAL-ORGANIC FRAMEWORKS; CRYSTAL-STRUCTURES; CO2 UPTAKE; LUMINESCENCE; ADSORPTION; PB(II); EXTRACTION; IONS; CONSTRUCTION; TEMPERATURE
Abstract: The complexes [Pb4L4Cl](n) (1) (HL = 4'-(4-(4-carbonylphenyl)phenyl)-2,2':6'2 '' -terpyridine) and [PbL'(NO3)center dot NO3](n) (2) (H2L' = 4'-(4-(3,5-dicarbonylphenyl)phenyl) -2,2':6'2 ''-terpyridine) were synthesized and characterized by single-crystal X-ray diffraction, elemental analysis, IR sprectra and PXRD. Complex 1 is a 2D coordination polymer with one-dimensional open channels in the size of 18.35 x 18.35 angstrom(2), while complex 2 has a coordination chain with an open channel. Both 1 and 2 can further stretched to a 3D supramolecular structure through pi-pi stacking interaction. The results of solid-state fluorescence spectrum at room temperature showed that complexes 1 and 2 exhibited blue light fluorescent property. They can be used as potential fluorescent materials that emit blue light.

Article Title: Systematic screening of DMOF-1 with NH2, NO2, Br and azobenzene functionalities for elucidation of carbon dioxide and nitrogen separation properties
Author Keywords: Metal organic framework; DMOF-1; CO2 capture and separation
Keywords Plus: METAL-ORGANIC FRAMEWORK; CO2; ADSORPTION; SORPTION; SELECTIVITY; CAPTURE; SITES; CH4
Abstract: In this study, dabco MOF-1 (DMOF-1) with four different functional groups (NH2, NO2, Br and azobenzene) has been successfully synthesized through systematic control of the synthesis conditions. The functionalised DMOF-1 is characterized using various analytical techniques including PXRD, TGA and N-2 sorption. The effect of the various functional groups on the performance of the MOFs for post-combustion CO2 capture is evaluated. DMOF-1s with polar functional groups are found to have better affinity with CO2 compared with the parent framework as indicated by higher CO2 heat of adsorption. However, imparting steric hindrance to the framework as in Azo-DMOF-1 enhances CO2/N-2 selectivity, potentially as a result of lower N-2 affinity for the framework.

Article Title: Lanthanide(III)-organic extended frameworks based on cubic [Ln4(μ3-OH)4] clusters: Syntheses, structures and application as fluorescent sensor
Author Keywords: Lanthanide complex; Coordination polymer; Metal-organic framework; Luminescent sensor; Fe3+
Keywords Plus: METAL-ORGANIC FRAMEWORK; MOLECULES; PROBE; IONS
Abstract: Three new lanthanide coordination polymers based on 4,4'-disulfo-[1,1'-diphenyl]-2,2'-dicarboxylate acid (H4DSDC) have been synthesized, namely {[Ln(4)(DSDC)(1.5)(COO)(2)(OH)(4)(H2O)(7)]center dot 10H(2)O}(n) (Ln = Tb, Eu or Sm), which are characterized to be isostructural. The cubic [Ln(4)(mu(3)-OH)(4)] species in these complexes are connected to adjacent one through coordination bridging from a pair of formate groups to generate double-cubane-shaped moieties as secondary building units, which are linked by tetraanionic DSDC4- ligands to form a 3D framework structure featuring (3(12).4(32).5(40).6(33).7(2).8)(3(2).4(3).5)(3) topology. The Tb(III) complex proves to be a highly selective and sensitive turn-off fluorescent sensor for Fe3+ ion.

Article Title: Synthesis and photocatalytic property of a new 1D metal-organic polymer
Author Keywords: Flexible carboxylate; Dye; Photocatalysis; DOS
Keywords Plus: COORDINATION POLYMERS; CRYSTAL-STRUCTURES; DEGRADATION; FRAMEWORK; ION; FLUORESCENCE; PERFORMANCE; ADSORPTION; REMOVAL; CD(II)
Abstract: A new coordination polymer having composition [Zn(L)(phen)](n) (1) has been synthesized solvothermally usingl,4-bis(3-carboxylbenzyl)piperazine acid (H2L) and 1,10-phenanthroline (phen) and Zn(II) salt. The single-crystal X-ray diffraction studies revealed that 1 shows a 1D chain constructed by linking [Zn(phen)](2+) units via L ligands, which further generates a 2D layer through strong pi center dot center dot center dot pi stacking interactions operating between the pyridyl rings of phen ligands and piperazine ring from adjacent networks along the c axis. The photocatalytic property of 1 in photo-degradation of methyl violet (MV) has been explored. The possible mechanism has been addressed using density of states (DOS) and partial DOS (pDOS) calculations.

Article Title: Microreactor-assisted synthesis of a nickel-based infinite coordination polymer and its application in the selective adsorption of alcohols
Author Keywords: Nickel; ICP material; Microreactor; Adsorption
Keywords Plus: METAL-ORGANIC FRAMEWORKS; RATIONAL DESIGN; NANOPARTICLES; CATALYST; MOFS
Abstract: Here, we report the synthesis of an infinite coordination polymer (ICP) with 2,5-furan dicarboxylic acid (FDCA) and nickel acetate as precursors in a flow tubular microreactor in a continuous mode. Compared with the available synthesis methods, which usually span hours to days at elevated temperature, this strategy remarkably saves time and energy, and greatly increases the efficiency of synthesis. It exhibits high stability to air and heat. Moreover, it shows excellent performance in the adsorption of alcohols.

Article Title: Two 2D isostructural coordination polymers: Syntheses, structure analysis and effective detection of Cr(VI) and Fe(III) ions in water
Author Keywords: Coordination polymers; Hirshfeld surface; Sensing ions; Competition absorption
Keywords Plus: METAL-ORGANIC FRAMEWORKS; CD(II) COMPLEXES; MOFS; REMOVAL; FE3+
Abstract: Two 2D isostructural coordination polymers (CPs) LM(L)(2)(H2O)(2)]center dot 2H(2)O (M = Cd2+ 1, Mn2+ 2) based on the multifunctional rigid ligand, 4-(3-pyrazin-2-yl)-1H-pyrazol-1-yl)benzoic acid (HL), were synthesized, characterized and analyzed with Hirshfeld surface. Compound 1 can potentially be used as a multi-functional luminescent sensing material for Cr2O72-, CrO42- and Fe3+ ions through luminescence quenching in water. And the K-sv values for these ions were estimated to be 1.23 x 10(4)M(-1), 9.26 x 10(3)M(-1) and 7.39 x 10(3) M-1, respectively. The mechanisms of quenching were also explored.

Article Title: Syntheses, crystal structure and property of a heptanuclear cluster
Author Keywords: Heptanuclear cluster; Azido; Crystal structure; Magnetic property
Keywords Plus: MICROWAVE-ASSISTED SYNTHESIS; COPPER(II) COMPLEX SYNTHESIS; METAL-ORGANIC FRAMEWORKS; SINGLE-MOLECULE MAGNETS; NICKEL(II) COMPLEXES; HETEROMETALLIC HEPTANUCLEAR; NUCLEARITY; DINUCLEAR; LIGANDS; FAMILY
Abstract: A new disc-like heptanuclear Ni(II) cluster (Ni-7(emmp)(6)(mu(3)-N-3)(6)]center dot(SiF6) (1) (H(2)emmp = 2-ethyoxy-6-methyliminomethyl-phenol), was synthesized and structurally determined by elemental analysis, IR, and X-ray single-crystal diffraction. Magnetic property of the complex has been investigated. The {Ni-7} core displays dominant ferromagnetic interactions from the nature of the binding modes through by the EO-N-3 and mu(2)-O. The latter molecule exhibits a unique planar core topology with 1:1.67 of the N-3(-) : Ni-II ratio.

Article Title: Mixed-ligand strategy affording two 6-connected 3-fold interpenetrated metal-organic frameworks with binuclear Co2II/Ni2II subunits: Synthesis, crystal structures and magnetic properties
Author Keywords: Binuclear; Interpenetration; Magnetic property; Metal-organic frameworks; Mixed ligand
Keywords Plus: COORDINATION POLYMERS; 1,4-BIS(3-OR 4-PYRIDYL)-2,3-DIAZA-1,3-BUTADIENE; DICARBOXYLATE LIGANDS; COMPLEXES; IONS; MOFS; CONSTRUCTION; TRINUCLEAR; DIVERSITY; GEOMETRY
Abstract: Two 6-connected (6-c) edge-transitive nets, namely, [Co-2(2,6-ndc)(2)(4-bpdb)center dot 2CH(3)OH center dot 2H(2)O](n), (1), and [Ni-2(2,6-ndc)(2)(4-bpdb)center dot(H2O)(3)center dot 2DMF](n) (2) (2,6-H(2)ndc = 2,6-naphthalenedicarboxylic acid, 4-bpdb = 1,4-bis(4-pyridyl)-2,3-diaza-1,3-butadiene), were synthesized under solvothermal conditions. The structure of 1 manifests a threefold interpenetrated 3D pcu topology based on paddle-wheel [Co-2(mu(2)-eta(1):eta(1)-COO)(4)] dimers. The structure of 2 possesses a three-fold interpenetrated 3D acs topology based on [Ni-2(mu(2)-OH2)(mu(2)-eta(1):eta(1)-COO)(2)(eta(1)-COO)(2)] dimeric units. Magnetic analyses indicate that both two compounds show weak antiferromagnetic interactions within binuclear Co-2(II) and Ni-2(II) units.

Article Title: Y Terbium metal organic framework: Microwave synthesis and selective sensing of nitrite
Author Keywords: Metal organic framework; Lanthanide; Microwave synthesis; Colorimetry; Luminescence
Keywords Plus: NITRATE; LUMINESCENT; HYDRATION; GEL
Abstract: The rapid and facile microwave method has been employed to synthesize [Tb-2(TTHA)(H2O4)center dot 9H(2)O (I; H(6)TTHA = 1,3,5-triazine-2,4,6-triaminehexaacetic acid) microcrystals. Based on the photoluminescent emission of I, which can be selectively turned off upon the coordination of nitrite, the selective determination of nitrite in water was developed without the use of Griess reagents. With the use of smartphone camera as a detector, the quantitative analysis of nitrite was conducted within the CIELAB colorimetric space, revealing the relative standard deviation of less than 5% for the working range of 3-12 mu g. Sensitivity, detection limit and quantification limit of the measurements were evaluated, providing the values of 0.732 (L-control/L-sample).mu g(-1), 1 mu g and 3 mu g, respectively.

Article Title: Two novel 3D MOFs based on the flexible (E)-1,4-di(1H-imidazol-1-yl)but-2-ene and multi-carboxylate ligands: Synthesis, structural diversity and luminescence property
Author Keywords: Metal-organic frameworks; (E)-1, 4-di(1H-imidazol-1-yl)but-2-ene; Structural diversity; Luminescent property
Keywords Plus: METAL-ORGANIC FRAMEWORKS; FUNCTIONALIZATION; DEGRADATION; ZN(NO3)(2); REMOVAL; SERIES; WATER
Abstract: Two novel metal-organic frameworks [Zn(btec)(0.5)(dib)]center dot H2O (1) (H(4)btec = benzene-1,2,4,5-tetracarboxylic acid, dib = (E)-1,4-di(1H-imidazol-1-yl)but-2-ene) and [Cd(btc)(dib)]center dot(C2H6N) (2) (H(3)btc = benzene-1,3,5-tricarboxylic acid) have been synthesized under solvothermal conditions. Complexes 1 and 2 were characterized by single-crystal X-ray diffraction, elemental analysis, IR spectra and thermogravimetric analysis (TGA). Crystal structure analysis reveals that complex 1 is a complicated three-dimensional (3D) non-interpenetrated porous framework, while complex 2 displays a 2-fold interpenetration 3D framework. The solid state photoluminescent properties of complexes 1-2 were recorded and discussed. [GRAPHICS] .

Article Title: The syntheses, structures, magnetic and luminescent properties of five new lanthanide(III) complexes based on tetrazole 1-acetic ligand
Author Keywords: Coordination; Tetrazole-1-acetic; Lanthanide(III) ions; Magnetism; Luminescence
Keywords Plus: METAL-ORGANIC FRAMEWORKS; CRYSTAL-STRUCTURES; COORDINATION POLYMERS; ND-III; LN; SERIES; STABILITY; ACID
Abstract: Five new lanthanide complexes based on tetrazole-l-acetic ligand and 2,2'-bipyridine as auxiliary ligand have been solvothermally synthesized with the formulas [Ln(2)(1-tza)(2)(NO3)(4)(2,2'-bipy)(2)] [Ln = Nd (1), Sm (2), Eu (3), Tb (4), Dy (5), 1-tza = tetrazole 1-acetic and 2,2'-bipy = 2,2'-bipyridine] and structurally characterized by elemental analyses, IR spectra and single-crystal X-ray diffraction. The single-crystal X-ray diffraction data reveal that complexes 1-5 are dinuclear structures constructed by nitrate-O-bridged and mu(1,3) carboxyl groups from 1-tza ligand, in which each nine-coordinated center Ln(III) ion is in a slightly distorted capped square antiprism geometry. The magnetic behaviors of 1-5 have been investigated. The solid-state photoluminescent measurements illustrate that complexes Eu 3 and Tb 4 display the strong fluorescent emissions in the visible region, whereas Nd 1 shows the characteristic near-infrared(NIR) luminescence. In addition, thermogravimetric analysis of Eu 3 is also described.

Article Title: Rapid synthesis of UiO-66 by means of electrochemical cathode method with electrochemical detection of 2,4,6-TCP
Author Keywords: Electrochemical cathode method; UiO-66; Carbon paste electrode; Electrochemical detection; 2,4,6-TCP
Keywords Plus: METAL-ORGANIC FRAMEWORKS; TEMPERATURE SYNTHESIS; 2,4,6-TRICHLOROPHENOL; MOF; SENSOR; COMPOSITE; FILM; NANOPARTICLES; FLUORESCENCE; DEGRADATION
Abstract: Electrochemical cathode methods were used to rapidly synthesize metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) UiO-66 and applied to electrochemical detection of 2,4,6-trichlorophenol (2,4,6-TCP). The effects of reaction voltage, time and temperature on the rapid synthesis of UiO-66 by means of electrochemical cathode method were systematically studied. It was confirmed that the UiO-66 synthesized by this method had small particle size with the diameter of 60 nm. Moreover, the UiO-66's performance in electrochemical detection of 2,4,6-TCP was studied. The effect of the content for UiO-66 in the electrode, the types of electrolyte solution, and the pH value of the electrolyte solution on the electrochemical detection of 2,4,6-TCP were systematically investigated. The minimum detection limit of this experiment could reach 6.49 x 10(-9) M (1.29 mu g/L), which is significantly lower than the one specified by the national standard: 10 mu g/L in drinking water. The limit of detection concentration is significantly lower than that of UiO-66-CPE prepared by conventional hydrothermal methods. Furthermore, in addition to 2,4-dichlorophenol (2,4-DCP) and phenol, some common cations and anions had only weak effect on the signals of 2,4,6-TCP with signal change less by 10%. This strategy provides specificity and sensitivity approach for the detection of 2,4,6-TCP and has promising applications in the water analysis field.

Article Title: Synthesis, crystal structure and magnetic property of a 3D Cu-organic framework
Author Keywords: Cu(II)-organic framework; Multidentate ligand; Crystal structure; Magnetic property
Keywords Plus: METAL; TETRAZOLE; WATER
Abstract: The assembly of Cu(II) ion and a multidentate pyridine-azole ligand 3-(tetrazol-5-yl)-5-(pyrid-2-yl)-1,2,4-triazole (H2TPT), has resulted in an interesting 3D non-interpenetrating metal-organic framework, [Cu(TPT)](n) (1). Compound 1 crystallizes in chiral P4(1)2(1)2 space group with Flack parameter of - 0.0268. The linkage of tetrazole groups of deprotonated TPT and Cu(II) centers generates the right-hand helical chains, and adjacent chains are further connected with each other, giving rise to a 3D intricate architecture. The compound was characterized by single-crystal X-ray diffraction, thermogravimetric analysis, elemental analysis, infrared spectroscopy and powder X-ray diffraction analysis. Moreover, the magnetic property of compound 1 has been investigated.

Article Title: Syntheses, structure and properties of an especially stable Cd metal-organic framework driven by benzotriazole-5-carboxylic acid
Author Keywords: Metal-organic framework; Solvothermal synthesis; Crystal structure; Chemical and thermal stabilities; Optical property
Keywords Plus: CONTROLLABLE SYNTHESIS; GAS-ADSORPTION; MOFS; LUMINESCENCE; PERFORMANCE; STABILITY; EFFICIENT; COMPOSITE; SENSOR; LAYER
Abstract: A new two-dimensional (2D) stable cadmium-organic framework, [Cd(btca)(2,2'-bpy)](n) (1), has been successfully designed and synthesized by means of solvothermal method (where H 2 btca = benzotriazole-5-carboxylic acid, 2,2'-bpy = 2,2'-bipyridine). Complex 1 has been characterized by combining single-crystal X-ray diffraction analysis, elemental analysis and IR spectroscopy. Single-crystal X-ray diffraction analysis reveals that 1 possesses 2D wave-like layered structure, and these 2D wave-like layers are interlinked each other by pi-pi stacking interactions to form supramolecular network. Compound 1 is especially stable in air, water, acidic/basic aqueous solutions (pH = 1 similar to 13) and common organic solvents. Furthermore, MOF 1 is stable up to 460 degrees C. Therefore, Compound 1 possesses excellent chemical and thermal stabilities, which makes it possible for practical applications. In addition, the optical property of the complex 1 was investigated.

Article Title: Two Zn(II) coordination polymers based on two isomeric flexible bis (pyridyl-tetrazolyl) ligands: Synthesis, structures and properties
Author Keywords: Metal-organic coordination polymers; Bis(pyridyl-tetrazolyl) ligands; Single crystal structures; Dye adsorption
Keywords Plus: METAL-ORGANIC FRAMEWORKS; CRYSTAL-STRUCTURES; ADSORPTION; LUMINESCENCE; PERFORMANCE; FLUORESCENT; BEHAVIOR; REMOVAL; DYES
Abstract: Two metal-organic coordination polymers (MOCPs) [Zn(3-bptzh)(BDC)] (1) and [Zn(4-bptzh)(BDC)] (2) were prepared by hydrothermal reactions of zinc(II) chloride with H2BDC (H2BDC = 1,3-benzenedicarboxylic acid) and two bis(pyridyl-tetrazolyl) ligands (3-bptzh = 1,4-bis(5-(3-pyridyl)tetrazolyl)hexane, 4-bptzh = 1,4-bis(5-(4-pyridyfltetrazolyflhexane). They were structurally characterized by single crystal X-ray diffraction, infrared spectroscopy (IR) and powder X-ray diffraction (PXRD). The 3-bptzh and 4-bptzh were firstly introduced into the metal-dicarboxylate synthetic systems. Complex 1 shows a 2D polymeric layer containing the [Zn(BDC)](n). ladder-like chain and [Zn(3-bptzh)](n) zigzag chain, representing a 3,5-connected {4(2).6.8(6).12}{4(2).6} topology. Complex 2 is a 3-fold interpenetrating network based on the 3,5-connected {4(2).5(2).6(5).7}{4(2).6} topological 2D framework including the [Zn(BDC)](n) ladder-like chain and [Zn(4-bptzh)](n) helical chain. The fluorescent behaviors and dye adsorption properties of complexes 1 and 2 have been investigated.

Article Title: An ultrastable {SiNb18O54}-based hybrid polyoxoniobate framework for selective removal of crystal violet from aqueous solution and proton-conduction
Author Keywords: Polyoxoniobate; Proton-conduction; Dye adsorption; Hydrothermal synthesis
Keywords Plus: METAL-ORGANIC FRAMEWORK; BUILDING-BLOCKS; POLYOXOMETALATE; DECONTAMINATION; NANOCLUSTERS; AGGREGATION; PERFORMANCE; SEPARATION; ADSORBENT; POLYMERS
Abstract: A novel inorganic-organic hybrid polyoxoniobate framework based on crescent-like {SiNb18O54} building blocks and [Cu(en)](2+)/K+ (en = ethylenediamine) linkers has been successfully made under hydrothermal condition. The compound is very stable under various conditions, and can selectively absorb crystal violet from aqueous solution. Additionally, the proton-conduction property of the compound was also studied.

Article Title: Synthesis of ZIF-8-based multifunctional shell and sustained release of drugs
Keywords Plus: METAL-ORGANIC FRAMEWORKS; ADSORPTION
Abstract: The combination of polystyrene spheres with porous ZIF-8 can induce the formation of a polystyrene @ZIF-8 core-shell structure. The polystyrene microspheres are then removed by an etching process to create a unique hollow ZIF-8. Finally, the adsorption process of the shell on small molecule dyes and drugs was studied.

Article Title: Facile syntheses of SOD-type tetrahedral tetrazolate frameworks for acetylene storage
Author Keywords: Metal-organic frameworks (MOFs); Zeolitic imidazolate frameworks (ZIFs); Tetrahedral tetrazolate frameworks (TTFs); Gas adsorption
Keywords Plus: METAL-ORGANIC FRAMEWORK; HIGH CO2; IMIDAZOLATE FRAMEWORKS; PORE OPENINGS; ZEOLITE; EFFICIENT
Abstract: ZIF-8 has become one of the most famous MOFs because of its high surface areas and chemical stability; however, the gas adsorption is unsatisfied in absence of active sites of its framework. In this work, we reported modified method to synthesize tetrahedral tetrazolate framework TTF-4 by using 5-methyltetrazole (5-Hmtz) to replace 2-methylimidazole (2-Hmim) in ZIF-8. Only by using DEF as solvent, TTF-4 can be steadily obtained in pure phase, which was proven by single crystal and powder X-ray diffraction. TTF-4 has similar surface areas and higher CO2 uptake than that of the former one and ZIF-8. More importantly, owing to the presence of uncoordinated N-sites of 5-mtz, TTF-4 exhibited higher C2H2 uptake (119 mL/g) than that of ZIF-8, which is also among the highest level of ZIFs.

Article Title: Two Cu-based cluster coordination polymers constructed from two thioether tripod tricarboxylic acid ligands: Synthesis, crystal structure and fluorescence sensing
Author Keywords: Coordination polymer; Crystal structure; Carboxylic acid ligand; Solvothermal synthesis; Fluorescence sensing
Keywords Plus: METAL-ORGANIC FRAMEWORK; FE3+; CO2; ADSORPTION; CR2O72
Abstract: Two new symmetrical tripod thioether tricarboxylic acid ligands, 1,3,5-tris(4-carboxyphenylsulfanylmethyl) benzene and 1,3,5-tris(4-carboxyphenylsulfanylmethyl)-2,4,6-trimethylbenzene (H3L and CH3-H3L) have been designed and synthesized. The reaction of two ligands with Cu2+ ions afforded two Cu-based cluster coordination polymers (CPs), [Cu3L](n) (1) and {[Cu(CH3-HL)DMF]center dot DMF}(n) (2). It was interesting to note that the substituent groups on central phenyl rings in ligands caused the bend tripodal and planar geometries as well as different coordinated modes for H3L and CH3-H3L, respectively, leading to different structures of CPs 1 and 2. 1 with monovalent Cu+ ions shows a 3D layer-stacking framework with hexanuclear [Cu-6(CO2)(6)] clusters, while 2 with divalent Cu2+ ions forms a 1D chain with dinuclear [Cu-2(CO2)(4)] paddlewheel clusters. 1 shows strong orange fluorescence and exhibits fluorescence sensing for Cr2O42- and Fe3+ ions with good selectivity and sensitivity.

Article Title: Ultrasound-assisted synthesis of a benzimidazole-containing Zn(II) coordination polymer as highly effective Lewis acid catalyst for cycloaddition of epoxides with CO2
Author Keywords: Coordination polymer; Catalyst; Carbon dioxide cycloaddition; Ultrasonic synthesis; Zinc(II)
Keywords Plus: METAL-ORGANIC FRAMEWORK; FIXATION; SITES
Abstract: A micron sized Zn (II) coordination polymer (CP), namely {[Zn(L)(5-mip)]center dot EtOH)(1) (L = 1,3-bis(benzimidazol-1-yl)-2-propanol and 5-H(2)mip = 5-methyisophthalic acid), was synthesized by ultrasonic irradiation at room temperature. The effects of ultrasonic power and time on the morphology and size of 1 were investigated in detail. Interestingly, micron sized 1 with considerable stability is can be used as an excellent and reused heterogeneous catalyst for carbon dioxide cycloaddition to epoxides under mild conditions.

Article Title: Control over the coordination preferences in Ag+ and Ag+/UO22+ 1,2,4-triazolecarboxylate frameworks
Author Keywords: 1,2,4-triazole carboxylate ligand; Silver(I) MOFs; Uranium(VI); Thermal stability
Keywords Plus: METAL-ORGANIC FRAMEWORKS; COMPLEXES; LIGANDS; TRIAZOLYL; POLYMERS; CRYSTAL; SERIES
Abstract: A new heterofunctional ligand (Me(2)trGly-H = 3,5-dimethyl-(1,2,4-triazol-4-yl)-acetic acid)was employed for the synthesis of two coordination polymers [Ag-4(Me(2)trGly-H)(2.25)(Me(2)trG1y)(1.75)(NO3)(2)](NO3)(0.25)center dot 6H(2)O (1) and [Ag-4(UO2)(H2O)(Me(2)trG/y)(4)(NO3)(2)]center dot 5H(2)O (2). In compound 1, the triazole functional groups interact with Ag+ forming the stable tetranuclear rhombic {Ag-4(Me(2)tr)(4)} motif, while the partially deprotonated carboxylic functions are left uncoordinated. NO3- anions are located between the equatorial positions of the Ag+ coordination cores resulting in 2D coordination layers. In a mixture of Ag+/UO22+ (compound 2) the triazole groups interact with silver(I) centers in the similar mode linking in a zig-zag chain. The COO- moieties show strict affinity toward hard Pearson's acid UO22+ that reveals a pentagonal bipyramidal environment {UO7} in a 3D framework. Analysis of thermal stability reveals the structure intactness of 1 till 100 degrees C and 2 till 180 degrees C. Loss of water molecules causes phase transformation, while total decomposition is observed above 230 degrees C.

Article Title: Sonochemical synthesis, crystal structure and thermal behavior of a new thallium(I) supramolecular polymer with hydrogen and bromine-oxygen halogen bonds
Author Keywords: Thallium; Halogen bond; Hydrogen bond; Sonochemical; Thermal behavior
Keywords Plus: METAL-ORGANIC FRAMEWORKS; TETRANUCLEAR CUBIC CAGE; COORDINATION POLYMER; IRREVERSIBLE REPLACEMENT; PRECURSOR; TL2O3; NANOSTRUCTURES; NANOMATERIALS; LEAD(II); SYSTEMS
Abstract: A new thallium(I) supramolecular polymer, [Tl(mu(5)-HTBT)(H2O)(])n (1), (H2TBT = tetra bromo terephthalic acid), with monoclinic crystal system and P2(1)/c space group has been synthesized and structurally characterized by single crystal X-ray crystallography. The coordination sphere around thallium(I) ion can be considered as O4Tl center dot center dot center dot O2Br3. Each HTBT- acts as a five-fold-donor ligand. Secondary hydrogen bonding interactions and Br center dot center dot center dot O halogen bonds also exist in 1. Microstructure of compound 1 was also synthesized with sonochemical procedure. Removal of coordinated water molecule from 1 was investigated in static atmosphere of air which showed different behavior in comparison with that obtained from its TGA (Thermo gravimetric analysis) in static atmosphere of nitrogen. These studies were confirmed with IR spectroscopy, TGA, X-ray powder diffraction (XRD) and scanning electron microscopy (SEM).

Article Title: A 3D cadmium(II) coordination polymer based on rigid ligand 1-tetrazole-4-imidazole-benzene: Solvothermal synthesis, crystal structure and tunable luminescent emissions
Author Keywords: Solvothermal synthesis; Cadmium(II) coordination polymer; 1-Tetrazole-4-imidazole-benzene; Tunable emission; Crystal structure
Keywords Plus: METAL-ORGANIC FRAMEWORK; WHITE-LIGHT; PHOTOLUMINESCENCE; COMPLEXES; FLUORESCENCE; EFFICIENCY
Abstract: Solvothermal reaction of CdCl2 center dot 2.5H(2)O and 1-tetrazole-4-imidazole-benzene (Htzib) yielded a new cadmium(II) coordination polymer [Cd2Cl2(tzib)(2)](n)center dot nH(2)O (1), which has been characterized by single-crystal X-ray diffraction analysis. In 1, metal center Cd(II) ions are linked by mu(2)-Cl and tzib(-) with mu(3)-kappa(3)N1:N2:N6 and mu(4)-kappa(4) N1:N3:N4:N6 coordination modes into a novel 3D structure. Due to the lattice water molecules filled in the closed cages of 1, they cannot easily escape from the 3D framework. Because of this structural feature, polymer 1 displays relative high thermal stability up to similar to 400 degrees C. Moreover, luminescent properties and theoretical calculations of 1 are also discussed. Interestingly, tunable ultraviolet-to-visible emissions for 1 are observed.

Article Title: Three new cobalt(II) coordination polymers based on 1,3-bis(4-pyridyl) propane: Syntheses, structures and magnetic properties
Author Keywords: Cobalt; MOFs; Crystal structure; Magnetic property
Keywords Plus: METAL-ORGANIC FRAMEWORKS; AZIDO-CU(II) CHAIN COMPOUNDS; CRYSTAL-STRUCTURE; SERIES; MONONUCLEAR; RELAXATION; DIVERSITY; BEHAVIOR; DESIGN; ACID
Abstract: Three dinuclear cobalt(II) compounds with different fluoro-substituted benzoate ligands, named as [Co-2(3,4-dfba)(4)(bpp)(2)](n) (1), [Co-2(3-fba)(4)(bpP)(2)](n) (2) and {[Co-2(2,4-dfba)(4)(bpp)(2)(H2O)]center dot(bpp)(H2O)}(n) (3) (3,4-Hdfba = 3,4-difluorobenzoic acid, 3-Hfba = 3-fluorobenzoic acid, 2,4-Hdfba = 2,4-difluorobenzoic acid, bpp = 1,3-bis(4-pyridyl)propane), have been successfully synthesized. In all compounds, Co(II) centers feature hexa-coordinated environments with distorted octahedrons. Among them, compounds 1 and 2 are isomorphic which perform three-dimensional (3D) network, whereas 3 displays a 2D layer structure. This modulation leads to different antiferromagnetic interactions between the metal ions (J(1) = -6.43 cm(-1), J(2) = - 2.28 cm(-1) for 1, J(1) = -19.44 cm(-1), J(2) = -6.08 cm(-1) for 2, J = -12.65 cm(-1) for 3).

Article Title: Au-nanoparticle loaded nickel-copper bimetallic MOF: An excellent catalyst for chemical degradation of Rhodamine B
Author Keywords: Ni-Cu MOF; Au nanoparticles (AuNP); Rhodamine B; Mixed linkers; Chemical degradation
Keywords Plus: METAL-ORGANIC FRAMEWORK; FACILE SYNTHESIS; PALLADIUM NANOPARTICLES; GOLD NANOPARTICLES; EFFICIENT; CHEMISTRY; DESIGN; FUNCTIONALITY; TEMPERATURE; ADSORPTION
Abstract: Synthesis, characterization and catalytic performance of Au-nanoparticle (NP) functionalized Nickel-Copper bimetallic three-dimensional MOF is presented. A three dimensional bimetallic MOF involving aromatic polycarboxylate ligands viz. benzene 1,4-dicarboxylate and benzene 1,3,5-tricarboxylate as linkers with Cu (II) and Ni (II) as metal nodes was synthesized through Solvothermal method. Structural and morphological studies of the as-synthesized material were carried out by FTIR, PXRD, SEM and TEM analysis. The elemental composition of the material was established by EDS mapping. Thermal stability of the as-prepared samples was tested by TGA analysis. The characterization details well establish the synthesis of first of its kind of bimetallic mixed metal-ligand MOF composed of nickel and copper metal ions trapped in an organic framework of bipodal and tripodal carboxylate based mixed ligands. The bimetallic MOF was successfully functionalized by Au NPs and was tested for its catalytic performance toward the chemical degradation of environmentally hazardous organic pollutant Rhodamine B. Compared to the pristine MOF, the Au doped MOF exhibited an exceptionally high catalytic activity (k(app) = 13.74 x 10(-2) min(-1)) and thermal stability, which can be attributed to the functional synergism prevailing between the Au nanoparticles and the three-dimensional bimetallic mixed ligand framework. The estimated k(app) value for RhB degradation is significantly better than those reported for various state of the art nanocomposite catalysts reported in the recent past.

Article Title: The synthesis of HKUST-1/SiO2 composite material based on 3D printing
Author Keywords: MOF; Silica ceramic; Composite; 3D printing; Complex shape; Catalysis
Keywords Plus: METAL-ORGANIC-FRAMEWORKS; AEROBIC OXIDATION; MOFS; REMOVAL; GROWTH; WATER
Abstract: We use photosensitive resin as material, and adopt 3D printing and pyrolysis to prepare silica ceramics. HKUST-1 was grown on the ceramic surface by step-by-step in-situ growth method to obtain the HKUST-1/SiO2 composite material. The HKUST-1/SiO2 composite material was characterized by X-ray powder diffraction (XRD), fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (FT-IR), scanning electron microscopy (SEM), energy dispersive spectrometer (EDS), thermogravimetric analysis (TG). The HKUST-1/SiO2 composite material not only has the characteristics of HKUST-1 and SiO2, but also can be designed into different complex shapes. In addition, the composite can be easy to separate from the product without centrifugation or filtration after the reaction is completed. The application of benzyl alcohol oxidation was an example to the performance of composite catalysts.

Article Title: Synthesis, characterization and photocatalytic properties of a Mn(II)-MOFs based on 2,2′-biisonicotinic acid
Author Keywords: Photodegradation; Methyl orange; 4-nitrophenol
Keywords Plus: METAL-ORGANIC FRAMEWORKS; CATALYTIC-REDUCTION; HYDROGEN EVOLUTION; DEGRADATION; NANOCOMPOSITES; 4-NITROPHENOL; CARBON; MOFS; LIGANDS; RARE
Abstract: In the present work, a 3D metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) of {[Mn-2(BPDC)(2)]center dot DMF}(n) was successfully synthesized via solvothermal method based on 2,2'-biisonicotinic acid (H2BPDC) as ligand. The synthesized complex was characterized by single-crystal X-ray diffraction, thermogravimetric analyzer (TGA), X-ray diffraction (XRD), Fourier transform infrared (FT-IR), X-ray Photoelectron Spectroscopy (XPS) and UV-vis diffuse reflectance spectroscopy (DRS). 4-Nitrophenol (4-NP) and Methyl Orange (MO) contaminants were selected as model contaminants to investigate the photocatalytic properties of the complex. In order to further evaluate the photocatalytic activity, the effects of the pH value and the catalyst dosage have been investigated. Under the optimized conditions, 97.72% of the photocatalytic degradation efficiency for MO was obtained. Moreover, only in 5 mins, the reduction efficiency for 4-NP reached 99.92% under the UV light irradiation. Accordingly, the results indicated that the superoxide radicals were main active substance in the process of photocatalytic degradation. It is worth mentioning that the complex could be recycled five times without noticeable loss of activity.

Article Title: Pyridine hydrazyl thiazole metal complexes: Synthesis, crystal structure, antibacterial and antitumor activity
Author Keywords: Pyridine hydrazyl thiazole derivatives; Transition metal complexes; Antibacterial activity; Antitumor activity
Keywords Plus: 8-MERCAPTOQUINOLINE
Abstract: The (thiazol-2-yl)hydrazone derivatives from 2-, 3-pyridine named (E)-4-(pyridin-2-yl)-2-(2-(pyridin-2-ylmethylene)hydrazinyl)thiazole (L1), (E)-4-(pyridin-3-yl)-2-(2-(pyridin-3- ylmethylene)hydrazinyl)thiazole (L2), and their three transition metal complexes named [Cd(L1)(NO3)(2)] (1), [Ni(L1)(2)(NO3)(2)] (2) and [Zn(L2)(2)(PF6)(2)] (DMF)(12)H2O (3) were synthesized and characterized by elemental analysis (EA), infrared spectra (IR) and single-crystal diffraction. Both complex 1 and 2 featured a mononuclear molecular structure, while complex 3 possessed an intricate 3D metal-organic framework. The antibacterial and antitumor activity of the ligands and complexes were tested. The results showed some compounds had absolute specificity for certain bacteria or cancer cell line, which implied a good application prospect in pharmaceutical use.

Article Title: Synthesis of MIL-100(Fe)/SBA-15 composite as a novel and ultrafast adsorbent for removal of methylene blue dye from aqueous solution
Author Keywords: Composite material; Porous materials; MIL-100(Fe); Adsorption; Organic dye pollutants
Keywords Plus: METAL-ORGANIC FRAMEWORK; WATER; ADSORPTION; WASTE
Abstract: A novel composite, MIL-100(Fe)/SBA-15 (1), was synthesized with hydrothermal method using SBA-15 mesoporous silica and precursors of MIL-100(Fe) metal-organic framework. The composite 1 was characterized fully and used for adsorption of dye solutions, including methylene blue (MB), rhodamine B, methyl orange and alizarine yellow. The results revealed that the composite 1 adsorbed 100% of MB molecules in 1 min, which is significantly higher than adsorption ability of bare SBA-15 and MIL-100(Fe).

Article Title: Synthesis, crystal structures and luminescence studies of zinc(II) and cadmium(II) complexes with 5-(1H-tetrazol-5-yl)nicotinic acid
Author Keywords: Coordination polymers; Tri-functional ligand; Metal ion; Topological structure
Keywords Plus: METAL-ORGANIC FRAMEWORK; SEPARATION; MOF
Abstract: Two coordination polymers (CPs) with novel tri-functional ligand, [Zn(H2O)(CH3OH)L](n) (1) and [Cd(H2O)L](n) (2), (H2L = 5-(1H-tetrazol-5-yl)nicotinic acid), have been synthesized and structurally characterized. Differently, 1 exhibits the 2D layer structure, while 2 exhibits the 3D structure due to the different connection modes between metal nodes and tri-functional ligand. The different coordination habit between metal ions and ligands must be responsible for the fabrication of versatile topologies. At room temperature, 1 exhibits an intense emission at around 367 nm, while 2 exhibits an intense emission at 358 nm. The different shift of the peak from free ligand, 1 and 2 must be assigned to the different configuration and pi-bonding of L caused by the different coordination environments of metal ions.

Article Title: A study on the catalytic behaviour of Cd(II) and Sm(III) coordination complexes towards the four-component synthesis of quinoline-3-carboxylates
Author Keywords: Metal-organic coordination compounds; Open metal sites; Lewis acidic character; Heterogeneous catalysis; Multicomponent reactions; Quinoline-3-carboxylates
Keywords Plus: METAL-ORGANIC FRAMEWORKS; HETEROGENEOUS CATALYSIS; HYDROTHERMAL SYNTHESIS; CHEMISTRY
Abstract: We report the synthesis two 3-dimensional coordination complexes namely, [Cd(2,5-Pydc)(2)(H2O)(2)]center dot H2O (1) [Sm (2,5-Pydc)(NO3)(H2O)]center dot(H2O) (2) using 2,5-Pyridine dicarboxylic acid (2,5-Pydc) as ligand by simple hydrothermal method. Nitrogen and oxygen atoms of 2,5-Pydc provided more scope for the coordination of Cd(II) and Sm(III) ions to the ligand in both the complexes with high dimensionality. The 3D networks of complexes 1 and 2 possessed attractive structures of supramolecular assemblies with good rigidity and high thermal stability. The coordinatively unsaturated metal sites in both 1 and 2 upon activation process generate a Lewis acidic environment. The Lewis acidic nature of complexes 1 and 2 was promptly utilised in the synthesis of novel quinoline-3-carboxylate moieties from the four-component single-pot fusion. Both 1 and 2 showed impressive catalytic activity in the formation of the products in high yield (92-96%) and in a short interval of time (15-25 min). The complexes 1 and 2 catalysed the Knovenagel condensation between aldehyde and active methylene group, leading to the generation of the reaction intermediate and target products with high selectivity. Optimisation studies confirmed that compound 2 showed superior catalytic activity over 1 due to the strong Lewis-acidic character of Sm(II). The method has potential as a low-cost, high-performance, green protocol for futuristic catalytic applications.

Article Title: Synthesis, crystal structure and photocatalytic properties of two 2-D coordination polymer constructed from pyridylmethylphosphonate
Author Keywords: Metal phosphonate; Nickel; Copper; Crystal structure; Photocatalyst
Keywords Plus: METAL-ORGANIC FRAMEWORKS; MN-II PHOSPHONATE; SINGLE-CRYSTAL; TRANSFORMATION; MOFS; CO; PHOTOLUMINESCENCE; HYDROGENATION; DEGRADATION; PERFORMANCE
Abstract: Two coordination polymers, formula [Ni(4-pmp)(H2O)(3)] (1) and [Cu(4-pmp)] (2), (4-pmp(2-) = 4-pyridylmethylphosphonate), have been hydrothermally synthesized and fully characterized. The two compounds display different two-dimensional layered structures because the 4-pmp(2-) ligand adopts different coordination modes. Compound 1 displays wave-layered structure constructed from single inorganic chain, in which each PO3 tetrahedron was corner-shared with two NiNO3 octahedrons. Compound 2 features layered structure built from double inorganic chain, in which each PO3 tetrahedron is corner-shared with three CuNO3 tetrahedrons. The photocatalytic properties of compound 1 show that it exhibits good photocatalytic activity in degradation of methylene blue (MB) and rhodamine B (RhB) organic dye.

Article Title: The transformation strategies between homogeneous and heterogeneous catalysts for the coupling reactions of CO2 and epoxides/olefins
Author Keywords: Carbon dioxide; Utilization; Coupling reaction; Cyclic carbonates; Heterogeneous catalysts
Keywords Plus: METAL-ORGANIC FRAMEWORKS; CYCLIC CARBONATE SYNTHESIS; COOPERATIVE CATALYSIS; PHOSPHOMOLYBDIC ACID; EFFICIENT FIXATION; PHOSPHONIUM SALT; PROPYLENE-OXIDE; IONIC LIQUIDS; DIOXIDE; OLEFINS
Abstract: CO2 as the C1 building blocks, plays an important role in the carbon cycle of natural. Various efforts have been devoted to the capture and utilization of CO2 with physical, biomass and chemical approaches. Among these methods, the coupling of CO2 with epoxides to prepare cyclic carbonates (CC) is considered to be one of the most promising approaches for conversing CO2 to valuable chemicals. Considering the strong economic potential of CC, it is urgently needed to improve the synthesis conditions and decrease production costs. However, CO2 is a thermodynamically stable molecule, the use of catalysts is therefore indispensable for activation and facilitating the CO2/epoxides coupling reaction in a selective manner under mild conditions. This review covers two kinds of homogeneous catalysts Lewis acid plus nitrogen/phosphorus organic compounds, and their corresponding heterogeneous catalysts mainly focusing on metal organic frameworks and porous organic polymers for the coupling reactions of CO2 and epoxides. Finally, an overview on the future trend of CC synthesis with alkene instead of epoxides to couple CO2 under relative mild conditions would be displayed.

Article Title: Multiresponsive luminescent Cd(II) coordination polymer for selective and recyclable detection of TNP and Cr2O72- in aqueous media
Author Keywords: Luminescent sensor; Coordination polymer; 2,4,6-Trinitrophenol; Cr2O72- ions
Keywords Plus: METAL-ORGANIC FRAMEWORK; MASS-SPECTROMETRY; IONS; CHROMIUM; CR(III); CR(VI); PROBE; NITROAROMATICS; SENSORS; MOF
Abstract: We report the solvothermal synthesis and fluorescent property of a novel luminescent coordination polymer (LCP) by choosing a new coplanar ligand, 2-(4-(3,5-dicarboxylphenoxy)phenyl) benzimidazole-5-carboylic acid (L). Single-crystal X-ray diffraction analysis reveals that the obtained LCP is formulated as {Cd(L-2}(n) (1) and features a 2D uninodal 4-connected sql/Shubnikov tetragonal plane net with {4(4).6(2)} topology. Fluorescence experiments suggest that 1 could work as highly sensitive and selective probe for both Cr2O72- and 2,4,6-tri-nitrophenol in water medium, resisting interferences from a variety of competitive anions or nitroaromatic compounds. The limits of detection for Cr2O72- and TNP in aqueous solutions were calculated to be 0.128 and 0.089 mu M, respectively. Just by a simple method, the fluorescent sensing ability of 1 could be regenerated.

Article Title: Constructing a 3D porous Co(II)-organic framework: Synthesis, characterization and chemical transformation of epoxide and CO2 into cyclic carbonate
Author Keywords: Co(II)-organic framework; Uncoordinated carboxylic acid; CO2; Catalysis; Cyclic carbonate
Keywords Plus: METAL-ORGANIC FRAMEWORKS; SELECTIVE GAS-ADSORPTION; CATALYTIC CONVERSION; LUMINESCENCE PROPERTIES; MOF; POLYMERS; CAPTURE; ACID; FE3+; FIXATION
Abstract: Metal-organic frameworks are booming development as porous crystalline materials and immensely attract lots of interest all around the world. A novel 3D Co-based MOF was successfully prepared by assembling Co(II) and H(5)tbdpb under solvothermal method. The as-made sample was investigated and characterized by many testing methods. Notably, uncoordinated carboxylic acids were reserved in the porous skeleton. By virtue of porous structure, CO2 adsorption capacity, and two catalytic centers of -COOH as Bronsted acid and Co(II) as Lewis acid, this MOF is able to high-efficiently fix CO2 and various epoxides to cyclic carbonates with preferable recyclability.

Article Title: Metal organic frameworks as water harvester from air: Hydrolytic stability and adsorption isotherms
Author Keywords: Metal organic frameworks; Water harvesting; Hydrophilic stability; Adsorption mechanism; Adsorption isotherms
Keywords Plus: LIGHT PHOTOCATALYTIC DEGRADATION; CATALYTIC PERFORMANCE; DEFECTIVE UIO-66; FACILE SYNTHESIS; GASEOUS TOLUENE; POTABLE WATER; OXIDATION; CO2; NANOHYBRIDS; SELECTIVITY
Abstract: The crisis of potable water is an important issue among the world's population. This is alluring the attention of researchers and become the pivot area of research into environmental chemistry. Researchers are looking to address this issue in water harvesting from the air in an inexpensive manner. Therefore, the purpose of this review is to find efficient materials for water harvesting which is an absorption-based passive process with adsorbing water vapour in the atmosphere that can be modified for high working capacity, pressure and temperature responses. Metal organic frameworks (MOFs) are promising tools to act as adsorbents for harvesting water from air to address the problem of drinking water in arid areas around the world. The present review describes the hydrolytic stability of MOFs and the chemical and structural factors that affect it. The degradation mechanism of adsorption and general characterization methods used for the study of MOFs are outlined. Here, kinetic and thermodynamic parameters affecting hydrolytic stability are also discussed. The adsorption /desorption mechanism in various MOFs have been discussed to address the role of functionalities and hydrophilicity. In addition to this water adsorption isotherms which give the idea about the performance of adsorbent with respect to adsorption/desorption cycle. Structural and compositional parameters such as organic ligands, metal nodes and defects which are required for altering adsorption/desorption behaviours of MOFs and to improve working capacity of adsorbent have also been taken into consideration. In future for efficient water capture, electrified devices incorporated with MOFs could be used to operate many cycles per day.

Article Title: Synthesis of two 3D supramoleculars and their fluorescent sensing for nitroaromatic compounds/Fe3+ ions in aqueous medium
Author Keywords: Supramolecular; Fluorescent sensing; Nitroaromatic compounds; Fe3+ ions; Aqueous solution
Keywords Plus: METAL-ORGANIC FRAMEWORKS; ZN(II) COORDINATION POLYMER; HIGHLY SELECTIVE DETECTION; STRUCTURAL DIVERSITY; MAGNETIC-PROPERTIES; CRYSTAL-STRUCTURES; PICRIC ACID; FE3+; CONSTRUCTION; LUMINESCENCE
Abstract: Two 2D coordination polymers (CPs), namely, {[Cu(bib)(2)]center dot 2NO(3)center dot H2O}(n) (1) and {[Zn-3(bib)(2.5)(C2O4)(3)(H2O)]center dot DMF center dot H2O}(n) (2) {bib = 1,4-bis (1-imidazoly) benzene} have been synthesized under solvothermal conditions. The structural analysis revealed that both 1 and 2 are 2D frameworks, which are further expanded into 3D supra molecular structures through C-HO hydrogen bonding. Luminescence properties reveal that 1/2 has highly sensitive and selective recognization for nitroaromatic compounds (NACs)/Fe3+ ions in aqueous solutions. Moreover, the luminescence quenching mechanisms were systematically revealed via photoinduced electron transfer (PET) process, resonance energy transfer (RET) and fluorescence lifetime.

Article Title: Synthesis of biaryl compounds via Suzuki homocoupling reactions catalyzed by metal organic frameworks encapsulated with palladium nanoparticles
Author Keywords: Heterogeneous catalysis; Homocoupling reaction; Metal organic frameworks; Palladium nanoparticles; Suzuki reaction
Abstract: Heterogeneous homocoupling reactions of phenylboronic acids were greatly accelerated via Suzuki homocoupling reactions. In this work, a tandem route was designed which firstly one part of phenylboronic acids reacted with iodine to form iodobenzenes, then another part of phenylboronic acids coupled with iodobenzenes to produce biaryl compounds. The tandem reaction were catalyzed by a bifunctional heterogeneous catalyst of metal organic frameworks encapsulated with palladium nanoparticles (Pd@MOFs). This strategy for forming symmetric C-C bond between benzene rings has obvious advantages such as high efficiency, easy separation, good recyclability and no addition of toxic halogenated benzene.

Article Title: Synthesis, structure and properties of a novel Cu(II)-MOF {[Cu2L(OH)]•DMF}n based on a semi-rigid polycarboxylic acid ligand
Author Keywords: MOFs; Cu(II); Rod-shaped SBUs; Semi-rigid polycarboxylic acid
Abstract: Metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) are coordination polymers with potential voids constructed by organic ligands and metal ions. In this work, we employed a semi-rigid polycarboxylic acid ligand 5-(4-carboxyphenoxy)methyl) benzene-1-thio-3-dicarboxylic acid (H3L) with the flexible -CH2-O- group between the two phenyl groups to construct a new Cu(II)-MOF {[Cu2L(OH)]center dot DMF}(n) (1). The structure analysis reveals that the adjacent Cu(II) cations are bridged by oxygens from OH- anion and carboxy group to get a one dimensional infinite rod-shaped secondary building unit (SBU). Furthermore, compound 1 exhibits an intriguing three-dimensional MOF based on infinite rod-shaped SBUs and L3-. PXRD result shows compound 1 is still stable after placed in air for three months. The variable-temperature magnetic studies indicate antiferromagnetic behaviors of 1.

Article Title: A water-stable Tb(III) coordination polymer based on 2-(4-carboxyphenyl)-1H-imidazole-4,5-dicarboxylic acid: Synthesis, structure, color-tunable fluorescence and sensing properties
Author Keywords: Lanthanide; 2-(4-carboxyphenyl)-1H-imidazole-4,5-dicarboxylic acid; Crystal structure; Color-tunable fluorescence; Fluorescence sensing; Al-3(+) ion
Keywords Plus: METAL-ORGANIC FRAMEWORKS; LUMINESCENT; SERIES; PHOTOLUMINESCENT; STABILITY
Abstract: A new water-stable Tb(III)-based coordination polymer (CP), {[Tb(HCpIDC)(H2O)(2)]center dot 2H(2)O}(n) (1) (H4CpIDC = 2-(4-carboxyphenyl)-4,5-imidazole dicarboxylic acid) was synthesized under hydrothermal condition, and characterized by single-crystal and powder X-ray diffraction analyses, infrared analyses, elemental analyses and thermogravimetric analyses. CP 1 exhibited a 2D (3,6)-connected kgd network with the Point Symbol of {4(3)}(2){4(6).6(6).8(3)} formed by HCpIDC3- anions mu(4) - bridging Tb(III) ions. The solid-state luminescent property of CP 1 was characterized and the results revealed that it exhibits fascinating excitation-wavelength dependent fluorescence property and may be a potential color-tunable fluorescence material. In addition, the luminescent emissions of CP 1 can be enhanced by addition of trace amount of Al3+ demonstrating its potential application for detection of Al3+ ion.

Article Title: Two new metal-organic frameworks: Synthesis, characterization, gas adsorption and simulation
Author Keywords: Nickel/cobalt-organic framework; GCMC; X-ray structure; DFT calculations; Topological analysis; CO2/CH4 separation
Keywords Plus: EWALD SUMMATION; BASIS-SETS; CO2; CONVERSION; NETWORKS; SORPTION; CAPTURE; 1D
Abstract: Two new Metal-organic frameworks, [Na1Ni3(mu(3)-OH)(mu(5)-BTC)(mu(6)-BTC)(H2O)(3)]center dot 4H(2)O (BTC = Benzene tricarboxylate ion) (1) and [Na1Co3(mu(3)-OH)(mu(5)-BTC)(mu(6)-BTC)(H2O)](3)center dot 4H(2)O (2) were synthesized under hydrothermal conditions and characterized by FT-IR, TGA, elemental analyses, single crystal and powder X-ray diffraction techniques. The porous structure of 1 and 2 were investigated by BET, crystal voids, topological analysis, gas adsorption and GCMC simulations. In the pressure range from 0.1 to 1.5 bar the adsorption selectivity of CO2 over CH4 at 273 K, 288 K and 298 K, is high in the activated MOFs. However, the adsorption selectivity reduces to 1.3 by increasing the pressure to 10 bar. GCMC simulations indicated probable interactions of CO2 around metal nodes and CH4 near the carboxylate groups. Experimental gas adsorption together with the GCMC simulation suggested 1 and 2 can be potential candidates for greenhouse gas capture or CO2/CH4 separation.

Article Title: Synthesis of a tetraphenylethylene-based metal-organic framework as the luminescent sensor for selective sensing of Cr2O72- in aqueous solution
Author Keywords: Metal-organic framework; Lanthanide-containing; Tetraphenylethylene; Luminescent sensor; Selective sensing
Abstract: A new metal-organic framework, incorporated with the tetraphenylethylene moiety as four-point connected node and Nd(III) by the self-assembly strategy, has been synthesized (denoted as 1, [Nd(HTCPE)center dot CH3CH2O](n)) and structurally characterized. The single crystal X-ray diffraction indicated that 1 contained a three-dimensional framework with infinite metallic chains. The porous feature of 1 shows the typical microporous adsorption of N-2 molecules at 77 K. The benign luminescence of the tetraphenylethylene-based ligand provides this material ability as potential sensor via sensitive luminescence response. The experiments indicate that 1 could be regarded as a selective luminescent sensor of Cr2O72- toward a series of anions in aqueous solution.

Article Title: A 3D copper(II)-sodium(I)-containing Strandberg-type phosphomolybdate-based coordination framework with a flexible bis (triazole) ligand: Synthesis, crystal structure and catalytic properties
Author Keywords: Metal-organic framework; Strandberg-type polyoxometalate; Crystal structure; Heterogeneous catalysis; Ring-opening polymerization
Keywords Plus: RING-OPENING POLYMERIZATION; METAL-ORGANIC FRAMEWORK; POLYMERS; BIS(TRIAZOLE); CLUSTERS; NETWORK
Abstract: A new copper(II)-sodium(I)-containing phosphomolybdate-based coordination framework, namely, {[EMIm] [Cu1.5Na(btmx)(2.5)(H2O)(2)(HP2Mo5O23)]center dot 0.5H(2)O}(n) (denoted as CZU-6, EMIm = 1-methyl-3-ethyl imidazolium, btmx = 1,4-bis(1,2,4-triazole-1-ylmethyl)-2,3,5,6-tetramethyl benzene), was synthesized by using ionic liquid EMIm-Br as a template under hydrothermal conditions. The X-ray structural analysis revealed that CZU-6 features the first example of 3D anionic polyoxometalate-based coordination framework with trinodal (4,4,4)-connected sqc topological net. Moreover, CZU-6 could be directly adopted as an efficient heterogeneous catalyst for the solvent-free ring-opening polymerization of e-caprolactone, and the catalyst could be easily recovered and reused several times without loss of its crystallinity and activity.

Article Title: Synthesis of two Cd-MOFs based on flexible trinitrogen ligand for CrO42-detection in harsh alkaline solution
Author Keywords: Luminescent metal-organic frameworks; Flexible thioether ligand; Structure; pH; CrO42
Keywords Plus: METAL-ORGANIC FRAMEWORK; COORDINATION POLYMERS; LUMINESCENT SENSORS; FLUORESCENT-PROBE; IONS; FE3+; CR(VI); WATER; NITROBENZENE; COMPOSITE
Abstract: A two-dimensional luminescent metal-organic framework (LMOF), {[Cd(tptb)2(H2O)2]center dot 2NO3}n(1), and a 3-fold interpenetrating three-dimensional framework with a new topology of 3,5-c net, {[Cd(tptb) (H2DOBDC)(H2O)]center dot DMF}n (2, H2DOBDC2- = 2,5-dihydroxyterephthalate; DMF = dimethylformamide), were synthesized and characterized based on flexible trinitrogen ligands, tptb (1,3,5-tris(4-pyridylsulfanylmethyl)-2,4,6-trimethylbenzene). Interestingly, compound 2 can not only potentially be used as a multi-functional luminescent sensing material for Cr2O72-, CrO42- and Fe3+ ions via luminescence quenching in DMA, but also can be as a highly selective and sensitive sensor for CrO42- at pH 13.0. And the luminescent quenching mechanisms also were explored. Such a Cd-MOF with good pH stability, water stability, interference immunity and regeneration ability can act as an ultrasensitive fluorescent sensor in the field of detection.

Article Title: In situ growth of NiFe MOF/NF by controlling solvent mixtures as efficient electrocatalyst in oxygen evolution
